title: Red Sonja: Hyrkania's Legacy - become the She-Devil with a Sword!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_7ZySSl0mk

Having enjoyed another Lynnvander Studios game, Daniel (@dungeondive) tracked down Red Sonja: Hyrkania's Legacy. He starts with a tour of the fiction. Sonja was created by Roy Thomas and Barry Windsor-Smith for Marvel, drawing on Robert E. Howard characters, and Daniel shows the six increasingly scarce novels by David C. Smith and Richard L. Tierney (Boris Vallejo covers, a Roy Thomas introduction). From there he digs into an Amra fanzine article reprinted in The Blade of Conan, Smith's Oron books with Clyde Caldwell illustrations, and Tierney's Simon of Gitta stories, which mix sword-and-sorcery with the Cthulhu Mythos.

The game itself is a hex-tile adventure. You explore outward from your castle, reinforce it five times before six despair tokens land, and defeat a scenario's big bad. He likes three things. Tile placement forces sensible terrain progression from plains to mountains, and a mountain ringed by six others becomes a peak. Dice combinations can be mitigated with Destiny tokens and equipment. And the action economy scales well: two heroes get six actions each. The adventure cards, 15 per region, add good flavour.

The drawbacks are near-identical characters with just one power (Ayla and Nais outclass the rest), unthematic equipment (Samaro's spiked flail doesn't exist as a card), and a rulebook with errors in two of the four scenarios, including an intro objective that is impossible under the rules. His verdict: a light recommendation, a C or B-minus game at a fair price.

----

How much does a game's source fiction carry it for you? Would you forgive Red Sonja's rough edges for the sword-and-sorcery flavour?
